I’m sure Dr. Nascimento is very smart and more than capable of becoming a great professor, but this lecture was terrible (worst I’ve ever attended). It seemed like she was speed running 

The pacing and lack of engagement really killed it for me. It made it near impossible to follow. As I stated earlier, the rapid pace and lack of engagement made it feel as though she was answering question N.A. for an expert rather than teaching a subject to a class.

However, overall these are understandable errors for a first time lecturer who may struggle with some social anxiety. But, it is my believe that having some form of social anxiety can be a positive as it allows you to empathize more with some students and eventually allow for better teaching. In conclusion, though I would bluntly state that was an awful lecture, I believe Dr. Nascimento possesses the necessary abilities and traits to become a great professor one day. I would just suggest she relaxes a bit, takes some breaths and pauses, asks the class more questions, and ultimately be more confident in her ability to teach. Just think of it as explaining a cool subject to some close friends rather than a job. I wish her the best of luck!

Cecilia did a wonderful job for her first attempt at holding her first lecture in such an intimidatingly large auditorium. She would benefit from slowing down her speech and emphasizing more important topics. I found it difficult to follow her lecture.

There is apparent rushing and discomfort with the material. I hope Cecilia learns the value of PAUSES. Pausing is a powerful tool to allow listeners to process the content and give her a natural break to breathe and think about what she wants to say next. If Cecilia replaced Um's and Ah's with paused, I am confident she will improve her speaking abilities dramatically.

Some other aspects of speaking she should pay attention to are rhythm, phrasing, tonality, and tempo. All of these factors play a role in delivering an effective lecture. I have no doubt that Cecilia knows the information inside and out, the next challenge is to practice practice practice!! It was a pleasure getting to sit in on your very first lecture. Good luck!!
